headline: Home Depot beat on EPS as bigger tickets offset fewer transactions; US comps +1.3% and FY2026 guidance reaffirmed.
guidance_note: Reaffirmed FY2026: comps ~flat to +2%, adj EPS ~flat to +4% vs $14.69; guide now includes IEEPA tariff refunds offsetting fuel/energy/input cost increases.
key_messages: Comps +1.7% (US +1.3%): average ticket +2.8% offset a 1.0% drop in comparable transactions.
Sales +5.7% to $47.9bn, lifted mainly by the GMS acquisition rather than organic demand.
Customers favored smaller repair/maintenance projects; larger discretionary remodels remain pressured amid housing affordability strain.
Recognized ~$730m of IEEPA tariff refunds in COGS/inventory; management sees rising fuel, energy and input costs offsetting them over the year.
Pro posted positive comps and outperformed DIY; CEO Ted Decker on temporary medical leave, CFO McPhail led the call.

consumer.big_ticket: Transactions over $1,000 reportedly rose ~2.4% (refrigeration, patio), but larger discretionary home improvement projects remained pressured.
consumer.pricing: Ticket up on mix and modest inflation; IEEPA tariff refunds (~$730m) recognized, expected to be offset by higher fuel, energy and product input costs.

macro_read: Home improvement demand is stable but skewed to small maintenance jobs; frozen housing turnover and affordability keep big remodels on hold, so housing remains a drag on durable spending.

sources.label: Zacks: HD Q2 earnings beat as sales, ticket rise

notes: About $730M of IEEPA tariff refunds were recognized this quarter; the per-share effect on adjusted EPS was not disclosed, so part of the beat may come from them.
